• ABB (Concalls): ABB India delivered an exceptional Q3 CY2026, marked by a 56% surge in orders to INR4,700 crores and a record INR13,000 crore backlog, providing strong revenue visibility through broad-based growth, particularly in Electrification. Despite solid revenue (+19%), EBITDA (+15%), and PAT (+10%) growth, the company navigates headwinds from inflation, commodity prices, and geopolitical factors, impacting margins and necessitating continuous pricing adjustments with a lag effect. A planned leadership transition with a new MD and CFO from January 2027 is underway, while the Automation segment faces cyclical project deferments, though no major red flags were identified beyond these common industry pressures. └ 📄 Source

• AARTISURF (Order Book): Aarti Surfactants Limited has received a customs order demanding approximately Rs. 1.28 crore in duty, along with equivalent penalties and interest, related to alleged import classification irregularities predating its demerger. This order further directs the confiscation of goods worth Rs. 5.22 crore (with a redemption option) and enforcement of bonds, establishing a material and unquantified financial liability. The company is evaluating legal remedies, but the long-standing nature of this dispute and potential for significant financial outflow represent a notable compliance risk. └ 📄 Source

• AARTISURF (Results): Aarti Surfactants Limited reported robust financial performance for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026, demonstrating substantial year-over-year growth in revenue and net profit. However, these periods were materially impacted by an undisclosed exceptional item of (430.03) Lakhs, which significantly reduced reported profit before tax. The financial statements received a clean limited review report from the auditors, while the company simultaneously announced the reconstitution of several key Board committees. └ 📄 Source

• AARTISURF (Results): Aarti Surfactants Limited reported robust unaudited standalone financial results for Q2 and H1 FY27, showcasing significant year-over-year growth in revenue and net profit. While an undisclosed exceptional item of Rs. 430.03 Lakhs negatively impacted Q2 profit before tax, the company maintained strong overall performance, receiving a clean limited review report from its auditors and reconstituting key board committees. The non-disclosure of the nature of the exceptional item could be a minor point for further inquiry, despite the otherwise positive report. └ 📄 Source

• ABCAPITAL (Insider Trades): Here is an executive summary of the financial document: Aditya Birla Capital Limited is seeking shareholder approval via postal ballot for material related party transactions totaling up to INR 4,950 Crores with its holding company, Grasim Industries Limited, for the current fiscal year (2026-27). While the resolution states these transactions will be on an arm's length basis and in the ordinary course of business, the document lacks crucial specific details regarding the nature of these substantial transactions. This significant lack of transparency concerning the type and specifics of such a large related party transaction constitutes a primary red flag for investors assessing potential conflicts of interest and the true financial impact on the company. └ 📄 Source

• ABFRL (Order Book): Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL) disclosed a demand order totaling Rs. 33.42 lakhs, including tax, interest, and penalty, from the Assistant Commissioner, Chennai-South, related to alleged discrepancies in credit notes and E-waybills. The company plans to appeal the order, asserting it is not tenable and anticipates no material financial or operational impact, though the substantial interest component, almost matching the tax amount, could indicate prolonged regulatory scrutiny or historical compliance issues. └ 📄 Source

• ACCELYA (Order Book): Accelya Solutions India Limited has filed an appeal against an order from the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner - II, which had mandated a payment of INR 2.72 crore related to provident fund proceedings. As part of this appeal, the company has deposited INR 68.13 lakh (25% of the ordered amount), indicating an immediate cash outflow and highlighting an ongoing regulatory dispute concerning potential non-compliance with provident fund regulations. └ 📄 Source

• ACI (Insider Trades): Executive Summary: Archean Chemical Industries Limited has formally notified the stock exchanges of its participation in the Kotak Midcap Conference on November 27, 2026, where company officials will hold meetings with analysts and institutional investors. This is a standard regulatory disclosure aimed at fostering investor relations, with the company explicitly stating that discussions will be based solely on publicly available information and no unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI) will be disclosed. There are no immediate material impacts or red flags identified, as this notification represents a routine investor engagement activity for a listed entity. └ 📄 Source

• ACEVECTOR (Insider Trades): AceVector Limited (formerly Snapdeal Limited) has successfully resolved a significant tax dispute, as the Hon'ble Delhi High Court dismissed the Income Tax Department's appeal regarding a ₹322.40 crore disallowance of advertising expenses for Assessment Year 2017-18. This ruling is a material positive impact, enabling the company to avoid a potential tax liability of approximately ₹111.57 crore and reinforcing its declared financial position. No red flags are identified, as the outcome is entirely favorable to the company. └ 📄 Source

• ACEVECTOR (Concalls): AceVector Limited reported robust H1 FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 17% year-on-year, primarily driven by a 31% increase in Snapdeal's fashion Net Merchandise Value (NMV) and 15% revenue growth from its Unicommerce SaaS platform, both leveraging AI-first strategies. While the company experienced an increased adjusted EBITDA loss for H1 FY27 compared to the prior year due to strategic growth investments, a significant red flag, it demonstrated a sequential reduction in losses by over 50% from Q1 to Q2. Management expects improved profitability and operating leverage in H2 FY27 as investment intensity moderates. └ 📄 Source

• ACMESOLAR (New Projects): Executive Summary: ACME Solar Holdings Limited has commissioned a 35.81 MW / 148.645 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) component in Rajasthan, with a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) secured with Tata Power and a Commercial Operation Date (COD) set for November 22, 2026. This represents a material positive impact by expanding the company's operational renewable energy assets and securing future revenue streams. However, it is noted that only the BESS component of the larger TATA FDRE Power Project is currently operational, implying further phases are still pending. └ 📄 Source

• ACMESOLAR (New Projects): ACME Solar Holdings Limited announced the commissioning of an additional 16.06 MW / 69.678 MWh discharge capacity for its FDRE Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in Rajasthan, with a Commercial Operation Date (COD) of November 22, 2026. This positive operational milestone advances the subsidiary's cumulative commissioned capacity to 175.72 MW / 733.939 MWh, demonstrating steady progress towards the full 250 MW project. No red flags are identified, as this update signifies continued project execution and movement towards revenue generation. └ 📄 Source

• ACMESOLAR (New Projects): ACME Solar Holdings Limited (ASHL) has successfully commissioned 57.69 MW of a Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE) project in Rajasthan, integrating 100.02 MW of solar capacity with a 57.69 MW / 265.38 MWh Battery Energy Storage System. This commissioning, with a Commercial Operation Date of November 21, 2026, marks a material operational milestone, initiating revenue generation under an existing Power Purchase Agreement with NHPC Limited and advancing the company's 250 MW project. No immediate red flags are apparent, indicating positive progress in ASHL's renewable energy development. └ 📄 Source

• ADL (Management Change): Archidply Decor Limited has announced the appointment of Mr. Devesh Daga as an Additional Director (Executive Director), effective November 13, 2026, to oversee key functions including marketing, business development, and operations. A significant red flag is his familial relationship as the son of the current Managing Director and nephew of a Non-Executive Director, which raises concerns about potential nepotism and corporate governance. Additionally, the document shows a notable discrepancy with the letter dated November 13, 2024, informing of an appointment effective two years later in November 2026, which is unusually early or a potential typo. └ 📄 Source

• AEROENTER (Fund Raise): Aeroflex Enterprises Limited has injected Rs. 10 Crores into its wholly-owned NBFC subsidiary, Aeroflex Finance Private Limited, to support the subsidiary's working capital, capex, and business expansion in tech-enabled lending. This significant capital infusion aims to capitalize on the subsidiary's recent substantial turnover growth in FY2025-26; however, previous year's financial volatility suggests a need for careful oversight of its performance. └ 📄 Source

• AEQUS (Insider Trades): Executive Summary: Aequs Limited Preferential Warrant Allotment Aequs Limited has approved a preferential allotment of 28,071,690 convertible warrants to Mellwood Trustee Services Private Limited, a promoter entity, raising INR 3.25 billion upfront and potentially another INR 3.25 billion by December 2027 upon full conversion. This transaction will result in approximately 4.18% shareholding dilution for existing shareholders and a significant increase in the promoter's stake from 14.99% to 18.40% post-conversion. While providing substantial funding, the concentrated allotment to a promoter merits consideration regarding its impact on ownership structure and potential shifts in control. └ 📄 Source

• AFFORDABLE (Concalls): Affordable Robotic & Automation Limited (ARAPL) reported a significant financial turnaround for H1 FY26, achieving profitability on both standalone and consolidated bases driven by robust cost optimization and operational efficiencies. The company is making a material strategic push into warehouse automation via its HUMRO subsidiary, evidenced by an approved 80 Cr investment and strong traction with US customers. A notable aspect is the promoter's interest-free loan of 26 Cr to fund the subsidiary, secured by selling his stake to HNIs, which while explained, presents a unique funding structure. └ 📄 Source

• AGASTYAEN (Results): Agastya Energy and Infrastructure Limited reported a marginal profit of 48.37 lakhs for Q3 2026, despite an alarming 90% sequential decline in revenue from operations to 288.26 lakhs. This profitability was achieved by an almost complete cessation of material purchases and significant expense reductions, raising concerns about the sustainability of its core business operations. Material impacts include a substantial reclassification of Property, Plant, and Equipment to assets held for sale and a large equity capital increase, collectively indicating a major operational restructuring or potential divestment. └ 📄 Source

• AGL (Concalls): Executive Summary: Allcargo Global Limited reported a significant financial turnaround in Q2 FY27, achieving net profitability (PAT of INR 32 crores) and substantial EBITDA growth (INR 122 crores), primarily driven by a 27% YoY revenue increase from elevated freight rates. This robust performance, achieved despite volume declines, was underpinned by strong cost control and strategic technology investments, though net debt saw a modest rise due to increased working capital. While current freight rate tailwinds are expected to soften, management is confident in sustained growth through ongoing business initiatives, with a historical bad debt provision anticipated to normalize. └ 📄 Source

• ALICON (Concalls): Alicon Castalloy Limited achieved record Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs. 652 crore, a 50% year-on-year increase (24% adjusted for alloy prices), driven by robust domestic market penetration, significant new program acquisitions in hybrid vehicles, and expansion into non-automotive segments. While broader cost inflation constrained reported EBITDA margins to 10% (12.1% alloy-adjusted), the company is focused on operational efficiencies and expects to maintain strong growth, supported by a substantial Rs. 6,700 crore executable order book and a new plant commissioning by April 2027. A minor red flag remains the challenging and currently unprofitable international operations, though improvement is anticipated. └ 📄 Source
